new.title: Hardware Resync configuration and command
new.contract: For a MIDI output with Sync enabled, the triangle next to the port name opens additional options. Hardware Resync selects a resync behavior when Resync External Hardware is enabled; when enabled, the Resync External Hardware button appears in the Control Bar and can be used to send resync messages to external gear. Drift during playback is a documented useful context, not an exclusive eligibility condition or a correction guarantee. The shared button versus per-port fanout and exact option-enable location beyond the named context remain unknown.

new.title: Hardware Resync symbolic mode roles
new.contract: The manual describes Stop and Start as the default resync behavior: a MIDI Clock Stop event followed by a MIDI Clock Start event. Start Only sends just the MIDI Clock Start resync event; Don’t Resync sends no resync messages. These symbolic source roles supply no byte encoding, total event count, spacing, timestamp, drift/phase correction, convergence or successful-device guarantee. Documentary default is not an exact-build constructor/reset/migration observation. Don’t Resync does not establish suppression of ordinary MIDI Clock traffic; per-output/all-output fanout and interactions with tempo, preroll, transport, Clock Type or Sync Delay remain unknown.

new.setup_and_action: In an independently admitted future build/platform and productive output-Clock/receiver context, explicitly enable Sync for the chosen output, expand its port-name triangle and inspect offered Hardware Resync choices. In a separate declared history explicitly enable Resync External Hardware, inspect its Control Bar button and invoke the offered command while retaining visible control state. No exact enable-option picker path, layout, shortcut, disabled/hidden-off presentation, port fanout or successful timing result is inferred. Mode traffic observations belong to separate null-oracle proposals.
